solved.q: Prepare the truth table for (p ^ q) v ~p.
steps: List all 4 combinations of p, q: TT, TF, FT, FF.
Column p ^ q: using AND rule, true only when both p, q are true: T, F, F, F.
Column ~p: negate p: F, F, T, T.
Column (p ^ q) v ~p: using OR rule (true if at least one is true): T, F, T, T.
solved.ans: Truth values of (p ^ q) v ~p are T, F, T, T for TT, TF, FT, FF respectively; it is a contingency.

solved.q: Examine whether the statement (p v q) v ~p is a tautology.
steps: List all combinations of p, q: TT, TF, FT, FF.
Column p v q (OR rule, true if at least one true): T, T, T, F.
Column ~p: F, F, T, T.
Column (p v q) v ~p: OR the two columns: T, T, T, T.
All entries in the last column are T.
solved.ans: (p v q) v ~p is a tautology.

solved.q: Using truth table, show that p -> q is logically equivalent to ~q -> ~p.
steps: List all combinations of p, q: TT, TF, FT, FF.
Column p -> q (false only when p=T, q=F): T, F, T, T.
Column ~q: F, T, F, T. Column ~p: F, F, T, T.
Column ~q -> ~p (false only when ~q=T, ~p=F): T, F, T, T.
Compare p -> q column with ~q -> ~p column: both are T, F, T, T, identical in every row.
solved.ans: p -> q is logically equivalent to ~q -> ~p (contrapositive law).

solved.q: Using De Morgan's laws, write the negation of: p ^ (q v r).
steps: Statement: p ^ (q v r).
Negate: ~[p ^ (q v r)].
Apply De Morgan's law ~(A ^ B) = ~A v ~B with A = p, B = (q v r): ~p v ~(q v r).
Apply De Morgan's law ~(q v r) = ~q ^ ~r to the second part.
Combine: ~p v (~q ^ ~r).

solved.q: Write the converse, inverse and contrapositive of the statement: 'If a number is divisible by 4, then it is divisible by 2.'
steps: Let p: number is divisible by 4, q: number is divisible by 2. Statement is p -> q.
Converse is q -> p: If a number is divisible by 2, then it is divisible by 4.
Inverse is ~p -> ~q: If a number is not divisible by 4, then it is not divisible by 2.
Contrapositive is ~q -> ~p: If a number is not divisible by 2, then it is not divisible by 4.
solved.ans: Converse: q->p (not divisible by 4 as above); Inverse: ~p->~q; Contrapositive: ~q->~p (equivalent to original).

solved.q: Write the negation of the statement: 'For all x belonging to N, x + 5 > 3.'
steps: Statement is of the form: for all x, P(x), i.e. (for all x in N)(x+5>3).
Negation of a universal quantifier statement is an existential quantifier statement of the negated predicate: there exists x such that ~P(x).
Negate the inequality: x + 5 > 3 negated is x + 5 <= 3.
solved.ans: There exists x belonging to N such that x + 5 <= 3.

solved.q: Write the dual of the statement: (p v q) ^ T.
steps: Rule for duality: replace ^ by v, v by ^, T by F, and F by T.
Given statement: (p v q) ^ T.
Replace v inside bracket by ^: (p ^ q).
Replace outer ^ by v, and T by F: (p ^ q) v F.

solved.q: Two switches S1 and S2 are connected in series. Write the logical statement for the circuit and the condition for the lamp to glow.
steps: Series connection corresponds to the AND (^) connective.
Let p: S1 is closed, q: S2 is closed. The circuit statement is p ^ q.
Lamp glows only when the statement p ^ q is true, i.e. the current flows only along a path with no open switch.
By truth table of AND: p ^ q is true only when both p and q are true.
solved.ans: Logical statement: p ^ q; lamp glows only when both S1 and S2 are closed (both T).

solved.q: Simplify the circuit given by the statement [p ^ (~p v q)] and draw the simplified circuit.
steps: Given expression: p ^ (~p v q).
Use distributive law: p ^ (~p v q) = (p ^ ~p) v (p ^ q).
p ^ ~p is a contradiction (always F), since a statement and its negation cannot both be true.
So expression becomes F v (p ^ q).
F v (p ^ q) = p ^ q, since F v A = A for any statement A.
solved.ans: Simplified statement: p ^ q, so the simplified circuit is S1 and S2 in series (switches corresponding to p and q).

solved.topic: Switching circuits - parallel and series combined
solved.q: Express in symbolic form and write the truth table for the circuit: S1 in series with (S2 parallel S3).
steps: Series corresponds to AND (^), parallel corresponds to OR (v).
Let p: S1 closed, q: S2 closed, r: S3 closed. The circuit statement is p ^ (q v r).
Build truth table: for each of 8 combinations of p, q, r compute q v r first, then AND with p.
e.g. p=T, q=F, r=T: q v r = T, so p ^ (q v r) = T ^ T = T (lamp glows).
e.g. p=F, q=T, r=T: p ^ (q v r) = F ^ T = F (lamp does not glow, since S1 is open).
solved.ans: Symbolic form: p ^ (q v r); lamp glows whenever S1 is closed and at least one of S2, S3 is closed.

solved.topic: Logical equivalence using algebra of statements
solved.q: Without using truth table, show that ~(p v q) v (~p ^ q) is logically equivalent to ~p.
steps: Apply De Morgan's law to the first term: ~(p v q) = ~p ^ ~q.
Expression becomes (~p ^ ~q) v (~p ^ q).
Factor ~p using distributive law: ~p ^ (~q v q).
~q v q is a tautology (always T), by the law of excluded middle.
So expression becomes ~p ^ T = ~p, since A ^ T = A for any statement A.
solved.ans: The expression simplifies to ~p, proving the equivalence.

solved.q: Prepare the truth table for p <-> q and state when it is true.
steps: List combinations of p, q: TT, TF, FT, FF.
Biconditional rule: p <-> q is true when p and q have the same truth value.
TT: both true, so p<->q = T. TF: differ, so F. FT: differ, so F. FF: both false, so T.
solved.ans: p <-> q has truth values T, F, F, T; it is true exactly when p and q have the same truth value.

practice.q: Construct the truth table for ~p ^ q.
practice.hint: Find ~p column first, then AND with q row by row.
practice.ans: F, F, T, F for TT, TF, FT, FF.
